headline: PM's flight from Japan delayed by nearly 5 hours; Tarique Rahman returns to Dhaka early Thursday
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's return flight from Japan was delayed by nearly five hours due to a mechanical problem, causing his arrival in Dhaka in the early hours of Thursday.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has returned to Dhaka after wrapping up a four-day official visit to Japan. His Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight landed at Shahjalal International Airport shortly after 2:45 am on Thursday.

The flight's departure from Japan's Narita Airport was delayed by nearly five hours due to a mechanical problem with the aircraft. It was initially scheduled to leave at 6 pm local time but departed around 11 pm.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Parliament Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni, and other senior officials welcomed the prime minister and his entourage at the airport's VIP lounge.

During his visit, Prime Minister Tarique held a bilateral summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. He also engaged with chairmen, chief executives, and senior officials from various Japanese private companies and financial institutions.
The meetings primarily focused on strengthening economic and trade cooperation between Bangladesh and Japan. A key objective was to expand Japanese investment within Bangladesh.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Parliament Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni, and other senior officials welcomed the prime minister and his entourage at the airport's VIP lounge.

During his visit, Prime Minister Tarique held a bilateral summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. He also engaged with chairmen, chief executives, and senior officials from various Japanese private companies and financial institutions.

headline: Bangladesh gets 3 more years for LDC graduation from UN, now set for 2029
summary: The UN General Assembly granted the extension for a smoother transition, allowing Bangladesh to strengthen its economy amidst global challenges.
details: Bangladesh has secured a three-year extension for its graduation from the Least Developed Countries (LDCs) group, moving the date from November 24, 2026, to November 24, 2029. This decision by world leaders at the 81st UN General Assembly aims to ensure a smoother transition amid risks from energy and supply disruptions. Nepal also received the same extension.

The government plans to utilize this additional time to attract investment, expand market access for local goods, and enhance port efficiency. Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir stated that signing trade deals with various countries and blocs will also be a priority.

Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, the prime minister’s adviser on finance and planning, emphasized the government's ongoing work on a transition strategy and urged the private sector to prepare through reforms. Key priorities include entering the trillion-dollar economy club, diversifying exports, and boosting productivity.

Mustafizur Rahman of the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) called the extension "critically important," expressing satisfaction that the global community endorsed Bangladesh's submission. He stressed the importance of using this time to graduate with momentum and ensure a sustainable process.

Rahman suggested revisiting the Smooth Transition Strategy (STS) given the extra three years, seeing it as an opportunity to shift towards an investment and competition-driven economy. He highlighted the need to reduce business costs and improve the overall business environment.

Mahmud Hasan Khan, president of BGMEA, welcomed the extension as good news but acknowledged persistent challenges. He emphasized the necessity of infrastructure development and crucial reforms to enable local industries to compete in the EU market post-tariff reintroduction.

Mohammad Abdur Razzaque, chairman of RAPID, noted that while the extension provides valuable time, readiness won't improve by time alone. He urged the government and private sector to act on urgent priorities with clear responsibilities, deadlines, and public reporting.

Razzaque identified restoring macroeconomic stability as critical for protecting export competitiveness, especially by bringing down persistently high inflation. He also stressed securing a trade arrangement with the EU, Bangladesh’s largest export market, as an early priority.

He further recommended export diversification, using LDC flexibilities to support new export sectors, and rationalizing the tariff structure. These measures should encourage investment and competitiveness to ensure a robust transition.
